steps.title: The Open
steps.content:
Hi, this is {{caller_name}} with {{provider_name}}'s office. Is {{contact_first_name}} available, please?

Hi {{contact_first_name}}. We're updating files for patients we haven't seen in a while, and yours came up. {{asked_by_provider}} Do you have a quick minute?

steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since you finished with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still feeling great, starting to come back a little, or pretty much back to where you started. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Doing Great
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes care with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still doing well.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Starting to Come Back
steps.content:
Thanks for telling me, {{contact_first_name}}. That does happen over time. Your notes say you were doing really well when you finished. Does that sound right?

(Let them confirm.)

steps.title: Fully Back
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. That's frustrating. Your notes say you were doing really well when you finished. What do you think brought it back?

(Let them answer. Be kind. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Doing Well: Stay Ahead of It
steps.content:
I'm glad you're still doing well, {{contact_first_name}}. Once things are going well, a regular check is what keeps a problem from coming back. Are you noticing any small early signs you'd like to stay ahead of?

(Let them answer.)

(No early signs: read the next line, then make the recommendation.)

The best way to protect your progress is a quick check now and then.

steps.title: The Transition
steps.content:
That's why I'm glad we connected today. Let me ask you a few quick questions so I can update your file. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me run through a few quick things so {{provider_name}} has the full picture. Okay?

(Ask one at a time. Acknowledge briefly. Note which ones are present. Do not dig in yet.)

Is the concern you originally came in for starting to come back?

Any related symptoms?

Is it getting in the way of everyday things?

Is it affecting your sleep, energy, or comfort?

Is it affecting you at work?

Is it keeping you from hobbies or time with family?

Are you frustrated or worried about where it's heading?

Is there anything coming up where you'd like to feel your best?

Do you wish you could get back to how you felt when you finished?

(Recap what they said, then ask:)

So {{contact_first_name}}, it sounds like the biggest things are (recap). Is that right?

Of everything we just talked about, which one bothers you the most?

(Their answer drives the rest of the call.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
(Take the concern they named. Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with work, at home, or relaxing and doing your own thing?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been going on a while, and it comes up more than once in a while. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: work, home, or your own time. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

And it sounds like you'd really like to get back to feeling the way you did when you finished. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, either way, it's worth a proper look instead of leaving it to chance. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look. If we can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. What would keep you from {{pt_uncover_action}}?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Objection: “I thought it was taken care of”
steps.content:
That's a fair thing to bring up. These things can come back over time. That's why a check-in makes sense, so we can see what's going on before it gets worse.

Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

Is there anything else on your mind?

steps.title: Objection: Cost or Insurance
Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That makes sense. That's something we can talk through at the visit, so you have all the information to decide.

Would that work for you?

steps.title: Objection: “I don’t have time”
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Life gets busy. The first step is one visit, and we'll work around your schedule.

Does that sound fair?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
That makes sense. Can I share a thought?

(Wait for the yes.)

Most people find it helps to come in for the look first. Then you both have real information to decide with, instead of guessing. Does that sound reasonable?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Scheduling
steps.content:
Great, {{contact_first_name}}. We have time this week on (day) and (day). Do mornings or afternoons work better for you?

(Let them answer.)

Perfect. I have (time) and (time). Which is better?

(Let them answer.)

Great, I've got you down for (day) at (time).

(Have two days and two times ready before the call, both within 48 hours.)

(Once booked, add your notes and press the green "Scheduled" button below to log the call.)
